Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Charithia usually hope their child will grow to embody joy of the lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: כריתיה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם כריתיה הוא שילוב של המילים כרית ויה, שפירושן מתנה וישועה. הוא מתאר אדם הנושא מתנות של חסד ורחמים מאלוהים, ומשקף ערכים של אהבה, נתינה ורצון טוב.

in_greek.name: Χαριτία
in_greek.meaning: Χάρις και αγάπη από τον Θεό
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Χαριτία προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις χάρις και θία, που σημαίνουν χάρη και θεία. Συμβολίζει το χάρισμα της θείας αγάπης και εύνοιας, και αντανακλά τις αξίες της πνευματικής γενναιοδωρίας και της αγάπης.

historical_references.reference: The monastic community of Chariton, founded in Egypt around 445 AD by Saint Chariton, was named after the saint himself and his sister Charitia who lived a virtuous life in solitude nearby. Charitia is mentioned in hagiographic texts as an exemplar of Christian asceticism and as a model of piety for monastic communities.

A 13th century Syriac manuscript from the Monastery of Mar Saba near Jerusalem contains a composition called the 'Book of Charitomartyres', which is a collection of hymns dedicated to several Christian saints including Charitia. This text suggests that Charitia was venerated as a martyr and her life story was passed down through oral tradition before being recorded in this manuscript.
